mostWorthwhile.text: Making the First star was most worthwhile: the cloud-to-star transformation felt consequential, and the explanation clearly distinguished nuclear fusion from an ordinary flame.

leastWorthwhile.text: Checking Pigment after it appeared was the least rewarding passage: it had no available partners and did not visibly advance the cosmic goals.

surprise.text: Gravity could not combine directly with Dust, despite the description of gravity gathering matter; later, the Dense cloud used Fire rather than Gravity to become a star.

arbitrary.text: Combining the First star with Air to make a Starfield felt somewhat arbitrary. The resulting image was evocative, but the role of Air in producing more stars was not clear.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see what stars contribute beyond light and how the game develops its living world, especially if it keeps distinguishing mythic combinations from scientific explanations.
